headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling can amplify Cognee’s sensitive support data into external web workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/crawl/agent endpoints, while Cognee processes documents and workflows. If Cognee consumes Firecrawl output without sanitization, attacker-controlled page text can become instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Cognee ingests Firecrawl markdown or scraped text as trusted instructions
IF Firecrawl is used on attacker-controlled pages and the output is forwarded into Cognee prompts
mitigations: Add a fixed instruction/data delimiter before passing Firecrawl output to Cognee
Strip or escape imperative phrases from scraped text
Require human review for any Firecrawl-derived content before agent use
Disable automatic chaining between crawl results and Cognee prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal, finance, support, and product-history data; Firecrawl handles web content and API keys and has broad network egress. If Cognee data is sent into Firecrawl for scraping, logging, or interaction, sensitive support data can leave the local boundary. The profiles do not show shared isolation or DPA controls, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Cognee forwards customer support or finance data into Firecrawl requests
IF Firecrawl logs or transmits request bodies containing Cognee session memory
mitigations: Do not send personal or finance data to Firecrawl
Redact secrets and identifiers before any Firecrawl call
Use a separate tenant or workspace for shared workflows
Turn off verbose request/response logging
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and Cognee has session memory while Firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support. If they write to the same workspace or shared mutable resource, concurrent updates can conflict. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the overlap is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or queue
IF Firecrawl MCP calls and Cognee session-memory updates target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid shared git or database state
Use per-agent credentials and storage
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped content and Cognee can store or transform it into decisions and workflows. If Cognee treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, downstream actions may propagate scraping errors or hallucinated facts. The pair has no documented verification step, so the risk exists even though direct action authority is not shown.
conditions: IF Cognee uses Firecrawl output as source-of-truth without validation
IF downstream workflows act on scraped facts or extracted fields
mitigations: Require a verification step before Cognee stores Firecrawl output
Compare scraped facts against a second source
Flag low-confidence extractions for review
Limit automated actions to non-destructive updates
requires-engineering: add schema validation and confidence thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal and finance data, while Firecrawl handles web content and API keys with broad egress. If regulated data is routed through Firecrawl, residency, retention, or processor obligations may diverge. No certifications or DPA details are provided for either agent, so the safest classification is a compliance-gap risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from Cognee is sent through Firecrawl
IF retention or logging policies differ for the same data class across the two services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Firecrawl workflows
Review retention settings for both services
Document data-flow boundaries and processors
Disable unnecessary logging of request bodies
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA and residency controls
